Definition: from G303 and G3306; to await:--wait for.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: the Thessalonians turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God, and to wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come. It is waiting with the eyes up — not idle waiting, but the waiting of people who have turned from idols and are looking for the Son.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for waiting carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the posture — turned from idols, serving the living God, and waiting for His Son from heaven.
